section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the work of refinement in the end of exile, especially through teshuvah, brings about the future revelation of "I will return in peace," and that this future revelation is already drawn down in a foretaste now.
section.t: And this is [the meaning of] "And I will return in peace to my father's house,"
which refers
(as above)
to the work of refinement,
through which is brought about
(is revealed)
the matter of "And I will return in peace," etc., which will be in the future, until "and this stone... shall be the house of G-d."
And this itself indicates the greatness of the elevation in the service of the end of the exile,
that the primary service then is the service of teshuvah (repentance)
(to the extent that even the service of Torah and mitzvos
(bread and garment)
at the end of the exile is after the precedence of the service of teshuvah
("And I will return in peace")205),
for through the service of teshuvah and good deeds
(meaning that even the good deeds are after the precedence of teshuvah206)
is brought about
(is revealed)
the matter of "And I will return in peace," etc., which will be in the future.
[To the extent that one hour of teshuvah and good deeds in this world is more beautiful than all of the life of the World to Come207,
because it causes something stronger than what is brought about through it.
And also because the pleasure of the World to Come is the pleasure of man, who is created,
whereas the pleasure of teshuvah and good deeds
(in this world)
is the pleasure of the Creator208].
And in particular,
that this—that through the service of now the revelation of the future is revealed—is in a manner that a foretaste of the future revelation exists also now
(as above in sections 24-25).
For since the service at the end of the exile is the service of teshuvah,
and regarding a baal teshuvah it is said142
"And it shall be, before they call, I will answer"140,
therefore,
also at the end of the exile
[and particularly when there is also prayer
("they call")
"And I will return in peace"]
there is already brought about "and I will answer,"
the drawing down and revelation of a foretaste of the matters of the future.
And analogous to Yaakov,
that while he was still in Charan, "the man increased exceedingly exceedingly, and he had many flocks"
(which is the main thing110)
"and maidservants and menservants and camels and donkeys"111,
so too is it with each and every Jew,
that at the end of the exile
(when they are in Charan)
there will be "and he increased exceedingly exceedingly,"
and in a manner of "I redeemed him in peace,"
in all interpretations and in all details,
both in spiritual service
[and particularly in the study and dissemination of Chassidus,
which will be without any confusions and with utmost expansion]
and in physical matters,
and in a manner of "and you shall break forth"209
("and he increased"),
that this will hasten and speed the future redemption—"I will hasten it"
(within the "I will hasten it" itself210),
that very soon there will be "an end to darkness"211,
and they will greet our righteous Moshiach,
who will lead us to our holy land,
"a land which... the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are always upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year"212,
the land of Israel within its borders,
and afterwards—and this too is in a manner of "I will hasten it"—"the L-rd your G-d will enlarge your border"213,
and very soon and speedily in our days214.
